references.text: The live goat (the Azazel goat) mentioned here is the same one introduced earlier in the chapter, where it is decided that one goat shall be sent out into the wilderness.
Describes the atonement process for the sanctuary, the tent of meeting, and the altar, which must be completed before the live goat can be presented.
Parallel use of כִּפֵּר (atonement) in connection with sacrificial acts and forgiveness of sin.
The atonement of the altar is an important element in the consecration process, also reflected in the ritual of the Day of Atonement.
Aaron shall make atonement on the horns of the altar once a year with the blood of the sin offering, which is linked to the annual Day of Atonement.
Ezekiel's vision concerning the cleansing of the sanctuary and atonement for the temple reflects the principles from Leviticus 16.
The book of Hebrews refers to the high priest's yearly entry into the Most Holy Place with blood to make atonement, which is fulfilled in Christ.
The cleansing of the tabernacle and all its vessels with blood points forward to the cleansing of the heavenly sanctuary through Christ's sacrifice.
